newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine slams Russia for detaining ship in Georgia.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine slams Russia for detaining ship in Georgia.

text.p: Ukraine on Thursday demanded that Russian border guards release a Ukrainian ship and its crew seized near Georgia's Black Sea port of Batumi.
Russian guards help to patrol Georgia's land and sea borders under a bilateral agreement signed in 1994 treaty.

"Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko summoned the Russian ambassador to Ukraine and stated our protest, demanding an explanation and the release of the crew and vessel," foreign ministry spokesman Yuri Sergeyev told Reuters by telephone.
Sergeyev said Russian border guards detained the "Almaz" with an 11-man Ukrainian crew and a cargo of citrus fruits on December 4 near Batumi.
Diplomatic sorces said radio communications had been cut off. Crew members were being kept in an unknown location while the captain was in detention.
"We do not understand why they (guards) did it," Sergeyev said. "We are also outraged by fact that we were not officially informed by the Russian side from the very start."

The row represented a blow to relations between the neighbouring former Soviet republics which are already strained by a five-year-old struggle to solve the issue of the former Soviet Black Sea fleet and its base at Sevastopol.
President Leonid Kuchma's top security adviser, Volodymyr Horbulin, also expressed dismay at the arrest of the ship.

"It's very surprising that the Georgian authorities displayed utter powerlessness. It leads to the sad conclusion that if the Georgians can do nothing about the Russian military in their own port, then we will to think very hard about Sevastopol," he told a news briefing.
Russia's upper house of parliament has approved a resolution saying Moscow should reclaim the port of Sevastopol -- though it is on Ukrainian territory.
Kiev sees Tbilisi as a "strategic partner" as the two countries have pro-Russian separatists to deal with -- in Ukraine's Crimean peninsula and Georgia's region of Abkhazia.

Ukraine recently concluded a deal with Georgia to reopen a ferry link between Odessa and Georgia's port of Poti. Kiev, dependent on Russian oil supplies, is hoping to get oil through Georgian territory from huge reserves in Azerbaijan.
